SMTO-AUT-0002 — An older result says an admin password couldn't be sent safely

GUID: 6005a29a-43d9-4ceb-81eb-5fce054cc140
Slug: privilege-transport-insecure
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: aut

What happened

  • This comes from a result saved by an older version of SMTO. SMTO refused to send an administrator password over a Gateway connection it couldn't confirm was secure. It doesn't mean your password was wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and find the Gateway the Task used. Check that it shows the Secure badge. SMTO only sends administrator passwords to a Gateway, the helper program that runs commands, whose secure connection it has confirmed.
  2. If it shows Insecure legacy or Identity changed instead, select Check connection and ask the person who manages SMTO to set up its secure connection. Those badges mean SMTO can't confirm it is talking to the right Gateway, so it won't send a password there.
  3. Once it shows Secure, check on that computer whether the step's work already happened, and only then ask SMTO in the conversation to run it again. The old result doesn't say whether anything ran, so checking first avoids doing the work twice.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Secure, and the step that needs administrator rights completes and is marked Elevated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select Forget trusted identity or turn off certificate checks just to make the warning go away.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A legacy result carries the privilege_transport_insecure kind: the selected Gateway connection could not be verified as secure for carrying sudo credentials. Current code reports more specific verified-route errors instead.

What this means

  • This legacy elevation-transport identity is retained for old/external payloads; current private-credential checks use more specific verified-route boundaries. No direct current producer was found for this compatibility identity. It preserves historical meaning without inventing missing cause, scope or execution facts.

Why this can happen

  • This legacy elevation-transport identity is retained for old/external payloads; current private-credential checks use more specific verified-route boundaries.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect any retained Gateway identity and transport readiness facts; do not reconstruct a destination from old exception prose.

How to fix it

  • This kind has no current producer; error_catalog/resolver.py maps it for old or external results. Confirm the Gateway has a verified TLS identity (Settings › Setup › Gateways shows Secure) and that elevation uses the current private sudo_password flow; never disable certificate verification or accept an unverified replacement identity to proceed.
  • Use a supported verified secure Gateway connection and the existing private credential flow. Never send the password through a command or ordinary prompt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The current authorized elevation flow establishes its required verified private route before credential use.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically disable certificate verification or trust an unverified replacement identity.
